decisions.reason: The inherited domain excludes m=0: def-binary-source-code-and-extension defines codes for the finite source [m], and def-finite-discrete-source-and-blocks explicitly requires m>=1. In a finite trie of a nonempty prefix-free code, each codeword has no proper extension among vertices, while every leaf is a prefix of a codeword and must equal it. The singleton case is one nonempty root-to-leaf chain. The page and contract preserve this nonempty-source convention; no edit is warranted.

Step 2.1 incorrectly attributes positivity of the input lengths to F2, which defines already-formed binary codes. Positivity is an explicit hypothesis, so the existence argument is sound and this is a nonfatal citation defect. Repaired the attribution to the hypothesis and explicitly applied F2 after allocation to its positive-length words. The published Kraft proof was read completely: disjoint cylinders prove necessity; finite free nodes of distinct lengths and maximal available depth give a computable prefix-free allocation. Finite requests need no choice axiom; nonsingularity then gives exactly the requested code. The Statement is unchanged.
